feature: Ask's score you can trust: an unseen test set, thumbs on rows, lookups counted
summary: Each of Ask's rows now has a quiet thumbs up and down; a thumbs down saves that request and its document as a test the eval has never seen. The eval has 42 such unseen requests (your two cat failures, poses, scenes, styles, edits, icons, layouts, redlines), reports them only as a total, judges every word of a request, and says how many drawings were looked up rather than drawn. Today's honest number: 20.1 on the unseen set, against 78.2 on the set runners climbed on.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Ask needs the local model it already uses.

try.do: On a blank picture press Ask, type "draw a cat curled up sleeping" and press the Ask button.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the Agent group, click the faint thumbs down at the right of the row "Drew a drawing".
See the thumbs down stay filled; click it again to take the vote back, or right-click the row for Good Result and Bad Result.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In Terminal run Scripts/ask-eval.sh feedback: your thumbs down becomes a new unseen case.
Run Scripts/ask-eval.sh report to see the climb and unseen totals side by side, with the share of drawings looked up.

Compare: this sheet is the set runners climbed on (78.2, every drawing stored or a coded scene); the unseen set's own sheet is at .ask-eval/held-out-runs/20261021-010309-ask-held-out/contact-sheet.png, kept out of queue/audits so runners never read it.

evaluate: Do the faint thumbs sit well in the row, or would you rather they appear only under the pointer?
Does 20.1 on the unseen set against 78.2 on the climbed set match how good Ask feels to you today?
Is "85% of drawings looked up, 27 of 33 drawing cases answered by lookup alone" the number you want every Ask change to report?
Are the 42 unseen requests the kinds of things you would actually type, and is anything you type missing?
rough: No mock covers the thumbs: they sit between the row's words and its switch because the row is what they judge, faint until picked (the hover-only version could not be clicked by a walk running behind other apps).
Three of the 42 unseen requests sat five minutes with the local model never answering and count as nothing made; filed as find-out-why-ask-sometimes-waits-five-minutes-fo.
In about one case in thirty a walk's click on Send did not start Ask; the eval now notices within 15 seconds and runs the case again.
A thumbs up is saved and counted but not turned into a test; only thumbs down become unseen cases.
The unseen set is held apart by a rule runners follow and by the eval never printing a case, not by anything that stops a determined reader opening the files.
The two cat requests the scene task listed as its climbing cases now belong to the unseen set, so that task climbs on a rabbit curled up asleep and a cat playing a guitar instead.
